classification.difficultyReason: Use a face's half-base and vertical height to establish the supplied pyramid formulas, then differentiate them and convert the shrinking side rate to metres per second.

content.prompt: A square pyramid has height twice its side length $s$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the volume $V$ and the surface area $A$ are $V=\frac{2}{3}s^3$ and $A=(\sqrt{17}+1)s^2$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\frac13s^2(2s)\\&=\frac23s^3.\end{aligned}$$
The slant height of each triangular face is
$$\begin{aligned}\ell&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2+(2s)^2}\\&=\sqrt{\frac{s^2}{4}+4s^2}\\&=\frac{s\sqrt{17}}2.\end{aligned}$$
Including the square base,
$$\begin{aligned}A&=s^2+4\left(\frac12\right)s\left(\frac{s\sqrt{17}}2\right)\\&=s^2+s^2\sqrt{17}\\&=s^2(\sqrt{17}+1).\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence find the rate at which $V$ and $A$ are decreasing when the side length is 4 metres if the side length is shrinking at 3 mm/s.

answer.short: Volume decreases at $0.096\text{ m}^3/\text{s}$; surface area decreases at $\frac{3}{125}(\sqrt{17}+1)\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$.
answer.worked:
$$\frac{ds}{dt}=-3\text{ mm/s}=-0.003\text{ m/s},\qquad s=4\text{ m}.$$
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dV}{dt}&=2s^2\frac{ds}{dt}\\&=2(16)(-0.003)\\&=-0.096\text{ m}^3/\text{s}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dA}{dt}&=2s(\sqrt{17}+1)\frac{ds}{dt}\\&=2(4)(\sqrt{17}+1)(-0.003)\\&=-\frac{3}{125}(\sqrt{17}+1)\text{ m}^2/\text{s}.\end{aligned}$$
The negative signs indicate that both quantities are decreasing.
